meta.thesis: AI agents are becoming customers. Businesses that blocked bots now have to win them.
meta.summary: This dashboard starts from a16z's B2A (business to agent) thesis, checks each of its numbers against the original source, adds independent context, and projects the main measures to 2030 under three scenarios. Move the year and scenario in the bar below and every view follows.

access.name: Browser use
access.text: The agent drives a browser, its own or the user's, and clicks through a site the way a person would. The article says most agent traffic works this way now.

access.name: Connectors, plug-ins and MCP
access.text: Agents call a business's tools directly with no interface to navigate. a16z calls this an app store for agents. Enterprise admins can already enable plug-ins for a whole organisation.

access.name: Lent identity and payment
access.text: Users lend an agent their identity or tokens, as with Sign in with ChatGPT, so sign-up and payment stop needing a person at each step.

access.name: Self-selected tools
access.text: Agents choose, install and pay for the tools they need with no human in the loop. At that point the agent is the customer.

winners.name: Agents and agentic models
winners.text: Standalone consumer agents, and every existing product once it starts acting for its user. ChatGPT's reach makes it the largest single opening.

winners.name: Products agents make possible
winners.text: Businesses that could not exist before, the way Amazon and Uber followed earlier platform shifts.

winners.name: Incumbents that optimise for agents
winners.text: Generative engine optimisation stops at being found. Agents go on to evaluate and to buy, so the prize is larger than visibility.

winners.name: Agent infrastructure
winners.text: Payments, fraud, identity and communication already strain at low agent volume, which is where new suppliers get in.

risks.name: People research with AI but will not let it pay
risks.text: In a Riskified survey of US and UK shoppers, 55% were not comfortable with an agent completing a purchase. In an Expedia survey, 8% were comfortable letting AI handle a travel booking.

risks.name: In-chat checkout already failed once
risks.text: Walmart saw purchases inside ChatGPT convert three times worse than clicking out to its own site, and OpenAI pulled Instant Checkout back in March 2026.

risks.name: Nobody owns the loss when an agent buys wrongly
risks.text: Card networks have no agent-specific dispute rule yet. One analyst expects the earliest in the April 2027 rules cycle.

risks.name: Protocol announcements outrun adoption
risks.text: A scan of more than 3 million sites found 26 public implementations of Google's commerce protocol by May 2026.

risks.name: Platforms can shut the door
risks.text: Amazon went to court over Perplexity's shopping agent. Sites blocked 17.5 to 21.3% of agentic requests in mid-2026.

risks.name: Four in ten agent projects may be scrapped
risks.text: Gartner expects more than 40% of agentic AI projects to be cancelled by the end of 2027.

model.short: US e-commerce driven through AI platforms
model.title: US e-commerce sales driven through AI platforms
model.desc: Sales that start on an AI platform. Most are still checked out on the retailer's own site.

anchors.scope: revised figure, seen as a chart title only
initiated, influenced or completed by agents

model.method: Starts at EMARKETER's revised 2026 estimate of $19.74B. The conservative path lands on EMARKETER's own revised 2030 figure of about $134B, the base path on the low end of Morgan Stanley's 2030 range, and the accelerated path in the upper half of Bain's range. Publishers define the measure differently, so the dots are not like for like. The 2025 point is derived from EMARKETER's December 2025 projection, which put 2026 at about four times 2025.

model.title: Automated share of web traffic
model.desc: All bots and agents as a share of requests. No published forecast reaches 2030, so this path is the dashboard's own.
model.method: 2025 is Imperva's full-year figure. 2026 is a single Cloudflare reading from June standing in for the year, on a different measurement basis, so it is classed as an estimate. The base path adds about two points a year, close to the 2022 to 2025 pace. The accelerated path assumes consumer agents add a further point or two each year.

model.title: AI agents in active deployment
model.desc: Agents running in organisations worldwide, on IDC's definition.
model.method: IDC expects more than 1B agents by 2029 and says that is 40 times 2025, which implies about 25M in 2025. The base path passes through IDC's 2029 figure. Gartner's count of more than 10B agents by 2030 includes agents made by individuals and governments and is listed below, not plotted.

model.title: Standalone AI agent software market
model.desc: Revenue of products sold as agents. Software with agent features built in is a far larger and separate number.
model.method: Two firms put 2025 at $7.8B to $8.3B and three put 2030 at $50B to $53B. Deloitte is lower at $35B to $45B. The base path follows the cluster of three, the conservative path lands on Deloitte's lower figure, and the accelerated path reaches $78B, the size Gartner gives for cross-functional agents in 2030 on a different definition.

model.title: Share of GitHub pull requests started by agents
model.desc: The article's leading indicator. No forecaster publishes a series, so this path is the dashboard's own.
model.method: The share went from 17% to 40% in six months. The paths assume that pace cannot hold and the curve flattens as it nears a ceiling: 62% by 2030 in the conservative case, 80% in the base case, 90% in the accelerated case.

model.title: Worldwide AI spending
model.desc: The compute, software and services bill behind the agent economy.
model.method: The base path applies Gartner's stated growth rates (36%, 21%, 18%, 15%) to its 2026 estimate, which reproduces its $5.95T figure for 2030. The band is 20% either side by 2030. The 2025 and 2026 points come from different editions of the forecast, and Gartner raised its 2026 figure between May and July.

sectors.name: Software and developer tools
sectors.mechanism: Coding agents choose and provision infrastructure, so the agent is the buyer in practice. Defaults, documentation quality and MCP support decide which vendor gets picked.

datapoints.metric: Pull requests started by agents
New Supabase databases launched by AI tools
Stripe CLI requests from agents

sectors.why: 2027 is when agent defaults start to redistribute vendor share.
sectors.winners: Backends agents reach for by default: Supabase, Neon, Vercel, Stripe, GitHub, Cloudflare. Agent vendors themselves.
sectors.losers: Tools that can only be set up through a GUI, seat-priced developer software, vendors absent from agent defaults.
sectors.risks: Dependence on one or two coding agents, and revenue from throwaway projects.

sectors.name: Media and publishing
sectors.mechanism: Agents and crawlers read content without sending a visit. Search referrals fall and revenue has to move to licensing, pay-per-crawl and direct audiences.

datapoints.metric: Google Search referrals to publishers
Media share of agentic traffic, largest sector that month
Weekly traffic lost by news publishers that blocked AI crawlers (Rutgers and Wharton study)

sectors.why: The damage is current. Offsetting revenue from tolls and licences is unlikely before 2028.
sectors.winners: Toll collectors at the network edge, publishers with loyal direct readers, owners of unique data.
sectors.losers: Small publishers that depend on search.
sectors.risks: Pay-per-crawl revenue is undisclosed, and blocking crawlers has cost traffic.

sectors.name: Retail and e-commerce
sectors.mechanism: Assistants become the discovery and comparison layer and send pre-qualified traffic. Checkout still mostly completes on the merchant's own site, and the contest is over catalog access and who owns the customer.

datapoints.metric: AI-referred visits convert better than other visits
Shopify orders from AI search, year over year
Agentic requests that reach checkout or payment
Walmart checkout inside ChatGPT vs click-out

sectors.why: Referral is material now. Delegated checkout waits on card-network dispute rules and wider protocol rollout.
sectors.winners: Catalog platforms, merchants with clean structured data, large retailers running their own agent inside assistants, card networks.
sectors.losers: Marketplaces that live on sponsored listings, thin affiliates, merchants whose product pages agents cannot read.
sectors.risks: Checkout inside chat underperforming, losing the customer relationship, and platforms blocking agents.

sectors.name: Advertising, marketing and search
sectors.mechanism: Answers replace lists of links. Budgets move to placements beside AI answers and to optimisation for models. When an agent picks the product, persuasion targets the model and the product feed.

datapoints.metric: US AI ad spend, 2026 to 2030
ChatGPT advertisers
Profound Series D, GEO platform

sectors.why: AI answers reach full distribution in search and chatbot ad inventory becomes self-serve.
sectors.winners: Google, GEO platforms, brands that third parties cite often.
sectors.losers: Classic SEO and affiliate arbitrage, and retail media if agents skip sponsored listings.
sectors.risks: Opaque measurement, and chatbot ad revenue running well below OpenAI's targets.

sectors.name: Financial services and payments
sectors.mechanism: Card networks add agent tokens, mandates and registries. Stablecoin rails target machine micropayments. In banking, agents that move deposits and shop for rates attack profits built on customer inertia.

datapoints.metric: Global bank profits at risk, most likely scenario
Real commercial volume on x402
US consumers who trust generative AI with payments (Visa report)

sectors.why: Rails are live but volumes are tiny or undisclosed. Deposit and margin effects follow in 2028 to 2029.
sectors.winners: Card networks, Stripe and Adyen, tokenisation providers, stablecoin infrastructure, fraud vendors.
sectors.losers: Banks that rely on low-rate deposits and issuers slow to support agent tokens.
sectors.risks: Liability is unallocated and crypto rails carry a lot of artificial volume.

sectors.name: Travel and hospitality
sectors.mechanism: AI is a major planning surface already. Booking is being wired in through apps and hotel partners, but travellers hesitate to hand over the transaction.

datapoints.metric: US travellers using generative AI for trip research
Comfortable letting AI handle the booking
Travel share of agentic traffic

sectors.why: Surveys disagree sharply on willingness to book through AI (44% in one, 8% in another), so delegation is unsettled.
sectors.winners: Online travel agencies and chains with inventory APIs inside assistants.
sectors.losers: Metasearch and content-led travel sites, properties without machine-readable rates.
sectors.risks: High cost of an error on an expensive booking, and loyalty lock-in.

sectors.name: Professional services
sectors.mechanism: Vertical agents do associate-level work, which moves pricing pressure from hours to outcomes.

datapoints.metric: Harvey funding round (secondary source)
Gartner: cut in cost-to-value gap of process-centric contracts

sectors.why: Tools are scaling. Agents acting as the buyer of services is still early.
sectors.winners: Vertical AI vendors and firms that reprice to outcomes.
sectors.losers: Firms whose model is billing junior hours.
sectors.risks: Liability for agent output. The figures here rest on single sources.

sectors.name: Logistics and supply chain
sectors.mechanism: Agents quote, book, schedule and track freight. Shipper and carrier agents begin to transact with each other.

datapoints.metric: C.H. Robinson: AI-recommended loads booked faster (company figure, best case)
C.H. Robinson: more on-time pickups (best case)

sectors.why: In production at the largest brokers, early across the rest of the market.
sectors.winners: Data-rich brokers and third-party logistics firms.
sectors.risks: Only vendor-reported best cases exist, with no independent data.

sectors.name: Telecom and connectivity
sectors.mechanism: Agent traffic changes the volume and shape of network load and creates demand for edge inference, bot classification and identity at the network layer.

datapoints.metric: Extra traffic per task when an agent executes it
Growth in daily AI-agent requests on Cloudflare
Cloudflare revenue growth

sectors.impactYear: 2027 at the edge, 2029 to 2030 for access networks
sectors.why: Edge and CDN platforms see it first. AI traffic is mostly text and small in bytes today.
sectors.winners: Edge and CDN platforms, network equipment vendors.
sectors.losers: Operators that carry the traffic without charging for it.

sectors.name: Small-business services
sectors.mechanism: Agents run the front and back office, the article's self-running small business. Use today is mostly individual productivity.

datapoints.metric: Small-business workers using AI at work
AI users automating workflows with little human involvement
AI-attributed Shopify purchases outside the top 100 categories

sectors.why: Adoption is wide but shallow. The long tail of niche merchants is already being found by agents.
sectors.winners: Platforms that bundle agents for small firms, niche merchants agents can discover.
sectors.losers: Small firms agents cannot see, local lead-generation intermediaries.
sectors.risks: Privacy and security worries, a skills gap and unproven returns.

sectors.name: B2B procurement and wholesale
sectors.mechanism: Buyer-side agents source, compare and reorder. Sellers need machine-readable catalogs, prices and terms. Coding agents buying developer infrastructure is the one live example.

datapoints.metric: Gartner: B2B spend intermediated by agents by 2028
Forrester: B2B decisions influenced by agents in 2027
Natural Series A, B2B agent payments

sectors.why: The large numbers are forecasts. No measured agent-executed B2B volume exists yet.
sectors.winners: Distributors with API-first catalogs, procurement suites, B2B payment and credit rails.
sectors.losers: Distributors that sell on relationships alone and vendors with opaque pricing.
sectors.risks: ERP integration and whether an agent has authority to sign a contract.

sectors.name: Healthcare
sectors.mechanism: Agents take on patient access, scheduling and back-office work. Consumer agents begin to touch provider sites. Regulated data slows autonomy.

datapoints.metric: Assort Health Series C
Agentic traffic to healthcare sites, month over month

sectors.why: Voice and scheduling agents are funded and growing, but delegation of regulated tasks is slow.
sectors.winners: Voice and scheduling agent vendors, providers with open scheduling APIs.
sectors.risks: Liability, privacy law and high-risk classification in the EU.

tech.name: Agent-native backend
tech.why: Databases, deployment and sandboxes that an agent can provision in one call are where B2A revenue is already visible.
tech.problem: The economics and security of short-lived resources that agents create, and dependence on a few coding agents.
tech.standards: MCP serves as the provisioning interface.

tech.name: Agent fraud and bot management
tech.why: Every site now has to tell a customer's agent from an attacker's, and blocking both loses sales.
tech.problem: Good and bad agents automate the same way. Up to 34% of the data fraud models rely on was missing in one in-chat checkout.
tech.standards: None of its own. Depends on Web Bot Auth and network agent tokens.

funding.what: Fraud signals missing in in-chat checkout

tech.name: Agent observability and governance
tech.why: Companies will not let agents spend or act for them without a record of what they did and why.
tech.problem: Evaluating multi-step agents in production and proving compliance.
tech.standards: MCP's 2026 roadmap prioritises audit trails, single sign-on and gateways.

tech.name: Agent-ready catalogs and storefronts
tech.why: An agent can only buy what it can read. Structured product data is the new shelf space.
tech.problem: Merchant data quality and slow merchant uptake of the new tools.
tech.standards: The ACP and UCP specifications for feeds and checkout.

funding.what: Shopify catalog-powered AI search converts vs general AI search

tech.name: GEO and agent experience
tech.why: Being the product a model recommends, then being the one an agent can evaluate and buy, replaces ranking on a results page.
tech.problem: Proving what changes a model's answer and whether it converts.
tech.standards: None. llms.txt is on 36,120 sites but 97% of those files are never requested.

funding.what: llms.txt files that get no AI requests

tech.name: Agent communications
tech.why: Agents need to call, text and email businesses and each other. Voice is the first channel to scale.
tech.problem: Authentication, spam and consent when agents contact agents.

tech.name: Network and edge for agent traffic
tech.why: The edge is where agent traffic is identified, shaped and, increasingly, charged for.
tech.problem: Charging for agent traffic. Pay-per-crawl revenue is still undisclosed.

tech.name: Agent payments and wallets
tech.why: An agent cannot be a customer until it can pay. Card networks, Stripe and stablecoin rails are all building for it.
tech.problem: Who pays when an agent buys the wrong thing. There is no network dispute rule, and volumes are tiny or undisclosed.
tech.standards: Visa and OpenAI aligned their protocols in June 2026. The x402 Foundation launched under the Linux Foundation in July 2026.

funding.what: Tempo mainnet and Machine Payments Protocol live
x402 transactions on Base, 87% under 10 cents

tech.name: Agent identity and know-your-agent
tech.why: A business needs to know which agent is at the door, who it acts for and what it is allowed to do.
tech.problem: Binding an agent to a person and a scoped mandate in a way every vendor accepts.
tech.standards: Web Bot Auth is an IETF working-group draft on the standards track, dated October 2026. It is not yet an RFC.

tech.name: Commerce and agent protocols
tech.why: MCP is already the default way agents reach tools. The commerce protocols that let them buy are a year or two behind.
tech.problem: Rival commerce protocols (ACP, UCP, card-network schemes) and MCP security, with more than 30 CVEs in early 2026.
tech.standards: MCP and A2A sit under the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation. UCP launched in January 2026.

funding.what: Servers in the official MCP registry
Public UCP implementations found in 3M+ sites

tech.name: Agent marketplaces and app stores
tech.why: The article's app store for agents: where an agent finds a tool decides who gets the business.
tech.problem: The assistant's owner controls distribution, and under 5% of public MCP servers are monetised.

funding.what: Public MCP servers that are monetised

tech.name: Agentic browsers and computer use
tech.why: Browser use is how most agent traffic arrives today, and it works on any site without integration.
tech.problem: Prompt injection, and the legal right of an agent to access a site at all.
tech.standards: None. Relies on Web Bot Auth for identification.

funding.what: Muse share of observed agentic requests

tech.name: Agent memory and personal context
tech.why: An agent that knows a user's preferences and history buys better, and whoever holds that context holds the customer.
tech.problem: Moving a user's context between assistants, and privacy.

tech.name: On-device and private agents
tech.why: Phone makers can put an agent in front of billions of people with the personal data already on the device.
tech.problem: A capability gap against cloud models, and regulatory access rules. Apple withheld its assistant from the EU at launch.

funding.what: Apple Siri AI announced, EU excluded at launch

tech.name: Machine-readable pricing and negotiation
tech.why: When both buyer and seller are agents, price lists, discounts and terms have to be published for machines and negotiated by them.
tech.problem: No shared format for terms, discounts or an agent's authority to commit. No dedicated funding found.
tech.standards: x402, which revives the HTTP 402 status code, is the only live standard for signalling a price.

method.note: This is an analytical product, not investment advice. Reported figures come from the companies and measurement firms named. Everything after 2026 is a forecast, and the dashed lines are this dashboard's own model, built to be argued with.
method.pipelineIntro: Each monthly edition is produced by a team of AI agents with separate roles, directed and signed off by the project's human designer.

pipeline.name: Article analyst
pipeline.text: Reads the source article twice and lists every number, claim, named company and linked source.

pipeline.name: Actuals researcher
pipeline.text: Opens each primary source, records the exact figure and period, and flags any mismatch with the article. Adds independent measurements.

pipeline.name: Forecast researcher
pipeline.text: Collects published forecasts for 2027 to 2030 and records only the years each publisher states. Nothing is interpolated at this step.

pipeline.name: Sector and technology researcher
pipeline.text: Gathers evidence by industry and by technology area: adoption data, funding, standards and open problems.

pipeline.name: Modeller
pipeline.text: Builds the dataset and the three scenario paths, anchored on the most credible published forecasts.

pipeline.name: Data reviewer
pipeline.text: A separate agent that did not build the dataset re-checks figures against sources and tests the model's arithmetic.

pipeline.name: Interface reviewer
pipeline.text: A separate agent tests the dashboard at phone and desktop widths, in light and dark, with keyboard only.

pipeline.name: Designer sign-off
pipeline.text: The human designer reviews both reports, decides open questions and publishes.

classes.text: Stated by the company itself or measured by a named firm on its own data. Checked against the original document where it could be opened.
A third-party estimate of a current value, or a figure derived from one. The derivation is given in the note.
A prediction published by a research firm or bank. Shown as stated, with the publisher's own scope.
Computed by this dashboard's scenario model. Changes with the scenario and assumption dials.
A score assigned by the analyst from the listed evidence, using the rubric on this page.

model.name: Three paths per measure
model.text: Each measure has a conservative, base and accelerated value for 2027 to 2030. Paths are anchored on published forecasts where they exist and say so where they do not.

model.name: Adoption pace dial
model.text: Blends between paths on a log scale. 0 is conservative, 50 is base, 100 is accelerated. The three buttons set it to 15, 50 and 85.

model.name: Friction dial
model.text: Shifts transaction measures later by up to 18 months, standing in for slow dispute rules, fraud losses or weak consumer trust. Only measures marked friction-sensitive respond.

model.name: Between years
model.text: Values between yearly points are interpolated on a log scale, which is what a constant growth rate within each year looks like.

model.name: Sectors and technologies
model.text: Scores and arrival years move one step, or half a year, with the scenario. They are judgement, not model output.

rubric: Pilots and funding, no measurable share of activity.
Agents measurable in discovery or traffic, under 1% of transactions.
Agents shape discovery for a meaningful share of customers and transactions are starting.
Agents are a primary channel and carry a material share of transactions or operations.
The agent is the default buyer or user, and vendors compete to be chosen by it.
limits: Several article figures have no link in the original. The most likely source is shown and marked partly confirmed.
Agent traffic shares come from single vendors measuring their own networks. They are not the whole web.
Bot traffic and AI agent traffic are different things. Most automated traffic is still ordinary bots.
Forecasters use different definitions of agentic commerce (executed, influenced, orchestrated), which explains most of the fivefold spread for 2030.
No published forecast was found for agent identity market size, agent-driven fraud losses or a yearly AI share of code. None is charted.
Some figures were read through trade press because the original was paywalled or unreachable. Those sources name both.
a16z has announced an investment in Wabi, one of the consumer agents the article names.
method.cadence: Updated monthly. Each edition replaces one data file, re-verifies the previous edition's figures and records what changed here.

data.result: Every source reference resolves, ids are unique and all counts match the update log.
Conservative, base and accelerated paths are ordered and rising for all six measures, and an independent re-implementation reproduced the base values.
68 figures matched the cited documents, including every number taken from the a16z article.
Relabelled from sales completed on AI platforms to sales driven through them, which is what EMARKETER measures. Its revised 2030 figure was added and now sets the conservative path.
A shopper survey was wrongly credited to Similarweb, one risk merged two surveys under one source, and three series pointed at documents that held only part of their data. All re-sourced.
A two-week claim about Meta Muse and two dated claims about Amazon blocking it had no cited source. Replaced with a sourced figure or removed.
One Gartner market figure was marked reported and is now an estimate. Seven source dates corrected.
Cloudflare's 57.4% is described as bots by its CEO and as AI agents in press coverage. Shown as partly confirmed.
Twelve figures could not be found on the page cited and 19 funding items were not re-checked this edition. OpenAI's own pages were unreachable.

ux.result: No sideways scrolling or clipped text at 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 pixels, in light and dark, across all six palettes.
Year, scenario, both assumption dials, play, filters, hash links and the dataset copy button all work without errors.
They could not be clicked with a mouse because an invisible layer sat on top. Reordered.
Headline tiles and chart values did not open a source. They now open the source, or the method for modelled values.
Heatmap text failed AA on levels 4 and 5 in several palettes and the dark ramp was not ordered. Ramp rebuilt per theme.
Accelerated had no effect on technologies, conservative pushed sector scores below today's, and friction moved the path outside its band. All three corrected.
1,000M now reads 1B, share changes show points, and missing years say no data.
Drawer now holds focus and locks the page behind it. Navigation, heatmap rows and tooltip use correct roles.
Year and scenario are not remembered after a reload, and there is no skip link to the timeline bar.

changelog.text: First edition. 26 signals, 6 context series, 6 modelled measures with 19 further published forecasts, 12 sectors and 15 technology areas.
